claim_text: The Japan App Store lists Parcel, id 375589283, with Japanese among its languages, Japan Post, Yamato, and Sagawa named, automatic Amazon ingestion once shipped, a developer claim that credentials stay on device, and a premium tier listed at 800 JPY per year that may vary. The fetched listing showed 4.7 from 323 ratings.
claim_status: directly observed within a stated scope
reasoning_summary: An independent tracker with Japanese carrier claims is offered, and a price is listed. The price is not evidence of payment.
limitation: Developer claims are not an audit, a merchant authorization, or a paid-user count. Four distinct rendered reviews are the review sample, not 323 ratings.
decision_implication: Benchmark C01 against Parcel, Gmail, and the carrier workflow. Retire both the empty-market claim and the zero-price-ceiling claim.

claim_text: The Amazon.co.jp Associates policies URL returned English Program Policies updated 14 April 2026. Participation Requirements 6(k) prohibits making orders or other transactions on an Amazon Site on behalf of any other person or entity, or authorizing, assisting, or encouraging that. The Japanese operating agreement was not opened.
reasoning_summary: The page chrome offers Japan and Japanese. The body and the operating-agreement link that came back are the amazon.com Associates central text. That is not a silent pass.
limitation: Not a Japan-wide statute against all agents. Not a reconciliation of the Japanese contract. User consent does not override the program if this text governs.
decision_implication: Do not book delegated Amazon affiliate revenue. Do not run an on-behalf execution test.

claim_text: Rakuten's affiliate guideline, updated 2025-06-26, states the 24-hour cart and 89-day completion rule, ordinary caps of 1000 JPY per item and 3000 JPY per user-month, an exception to both caps for rate-up products, a prohibition on using the program to provide a competing or potentially competing service, and a prohibition on results without a click.
claim_status: directly observed within a stated scope
reasoning_summary: v1 was wrong to treat the window as secondary-only. The competing-service clause is specific and unresolved for this product.
limitation: Rate-up eligibility is unpublished and not assumed. The corporate partner agreement was not read. Different-device attribution does not authorize the startup to purchase.
decision_implication: Eligibility before rate. Ordinary caps apply unless a rate-up entitlement is actually held.

decision_implication: Retire generic in-chat checkout as the architecture. Leave other purchase-assistance designs unresolved.
